rationale: The first reply correctly identified moisture on the spark electrodes after wet cleaning, advised isolating and drying, and checking burner caps, which matches the hidden truth. The second reply misread 'unplugged the hob plug under the sink' as water near the plug/socket and issued a boilerplate stop-use/electrician warning ('don't use the machine again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has checked it') that the customer's evidence did not support, then contradicted itself with 'That's excellent news'. It never told the customer to simply reconnect once dry and only seek an engineer if clicking persists, and the repeated 'Enter your model number' replacement panel was irrelevant to a no-part-needed case.
